body:
Point 1 - moved to #2910

> 11.1.1 Verify that there is an explicit policy for management of cryptographic keys and that a cryptographic key lifecycle follows a key management standard such as NIST SP 800-57. How do you verify that? Documented security decision?

--- Point 2 > 11.1.2 Verify that a cryptographic inventory is performed, maintained, regularly updated, and includes all cryptographic keys, algorithms, and certificates used by the application. It must also document where keys can and cannot be used in the system and also the types of data which can and cannot be protected using the keys. 2x also --- Point 3 > 11.5.1 Verify that all random numbers and strings which are intended to be non-guessable must be generated using a cryptographically-secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) and have at least 128 bits of entropy. Note that UUIDs do not respect this condition. "cryptographically-secure" > "cryptographically secure"? ---
Point 4 - moved to #2911

> 11.5.2 Verify that random number generation continues to work securely, even under heavy system load, or that the system degrades gracefully. Is it verifiable in practice?

--- Point 5 V11.8 Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Maybe the title should be without acronym? > V11.8 Post-Quantum Cryptography ---
Point 6 - moved to #2912

> 11.8.1 Verify that a cryptographic inventory is maintained and includes a documented transformation plan or mapping that outlines the migration path from current cryptographic algorithms and systems to those that use post-quantum cryptography. > 11.8.2 Verify that advancements in the field of post-quantum cryptography are being monitored in order to ensure that the application is aligned with emerging industry standards, and remains prepared for quantum threats. Those are not implementation requirements that you can check from the application. This seems like a requirement for V11.1 section, precondition for 11.2.2?

comments.body: ping @randomstuff (I can not assign issue to you before you are not involved with the issue, but I can tag you...)

> [11.1.1] How do you verify that? Documented security decision?

Yes I guess. I am not so sure about this requirement. I would be tempted to merge this one into the 11.1.2:

> Verify that a cryptographic inventory is performed, maintained, regularly updated, and includes all cryptographic keys, algorithms, and certificates used by the application. It must also document where keys can and cannot be used in the system, their lifetime and management policy also the types of data which can and cannot be protected using the keys.

but that may be a bad idea.

***

> "cryptographically-secure" > "cryptographically secure"?

Yes apparently, that's the correct way.

***

> > 11.5.2 Verify that random number generation continues to work securely, even under heavy system load, or that the system degrades gracefully.
>
> Is it verifiable in practice?

I agree that may not be easy to verify. (Or that the verifier may be left wondering what he is supposed to do about that requirement.)

***

> > V11.8 Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC)
>
> Maybe the title should be without acronym?

Agree.

***

[11.8.1 and 11.8.2]

> Those are not implementation requirements that you can check from the application.

Yes, I agree.
Big discussions are moved to separate issues, tiny changes are addressed in #2908
